puzzle.body: All the matchers should implement describeMismatchSafely and their tests must verify that the implementation of the descriptions are satisfactory. The matchers should not expose publicly the xxxSafely method and the tests should rely on actual real use with assertThat. See ScalarHasValueTest for an example of a satisfactory result.
puzzle.author: Victor Noël

puzzle.body:
The TextMatcherEnvelope should support the description for actual/expected values separately. For example, for now we are using single `TextMatcherEnvelope#TextMatcherEnvelope(Matcher, String)` description object which describe actual/expected objects and leads to uninformative message in case of failure of MatchesRegexp. For example 
{@code java.lang.AssertionError: Expected: Text matches "^.*know\sit\.$" but: Text matches "I'm simple." }
Its better to have this error message 
{@code java.lang.AssertionError: Expected: Text matches "^.*know\sit\.$" but: Text is "I'm simple." }
puzzle.author: Yurii Dubinka

puzzle.body: This plugin execution was disabled (phase was set to `package` before) because it prevents cactoos from actually using cactoos-matchers since the interfaces provided by cactoos (`Text`, `Func`, `Scalar`, etc) and those expected by cactoos-matchers do no match!
